title: Renewal Terms for VPS and Dedicated Servers
content:
**1. When a renewal may be charged.** A renewal may be charged only while the server status is active or suspended.

**2. What a renewal is billed at.** A renewal is billed at the tier's price for the renewal term plus the active add-ons for the same months, less any applicable account discount, and the new term starts on the previous term end date.

**3. Auto-renew timing.** Where auto-renew is on, the renewal is charged the tier's auto-renew charging lead, in days, before the term end date, and an unpaid server keeps running for the tier's grace days, in calendar days, after the term end before suspension.

These clauses apply to every server in the VPS and Dedicated Servers range.

## Status of the server and whether a renewal may be charged

| Server status on the holding record | Renewal may be charged |
|---|---|
| Active | Yes |
| Suspended | Yes |
| Provisioning | No |
| Cancel pending | No |
| Cancelled | No |
| Terminated | No |

The evidence is the status of that server on its own holding record, not the customer's description of it.

## The renewed term

- The renewal line covers the new term: it runs from the previous term end date to the new term end date, and records the months covered.
- The new term end date is the new term start plus the renewal term in calendar months.
- A renewal line is recorded either as a renewal or as an auto-renew charge.
- A renewal attempt that is declined is recorded in the server's service history as a declined attempt.

## Hypothetical timing illustration

The lead time below is an invented input, not a Harborline figure. For a server whose term ends on 20 June and a hypothetical lead time of 6 days, an auto-renew charge falls on 14 June, six calendar days before the term end date. The new term starts on 20 June, the previous term end date.
